# Anti-Slop Gate

Significant code changes MUST pass an anti-slop review before being declared complete.

## When to Trigger

Run `/anti-slop` (or dispatch the triad: uncle-bob + linus-torvalds + el-demoledor) when:
- Adding or modifying >50 lines of logic across 2+ files
- Creating new modules, handlers, or architectural boundaries
- Refactoring existing code (verify the refactor didn't introduce new slop)
- Any PR that touches core domain logic

## What to Look For

The anti-slop audit catches:
- **DRY violations**: duplicated validation/business rules across paths (e.g., blur vs submit validators)
- **Shallow modules**: wrappers that hide nothing, forwarding-only layers
- **Input boundary gaps**: missing sanitization at form/API/CLI input boundaries
- **Dead code**: functions/exports with zero consumers
- **Fake architecture**: folder structure that implies boundaries but imports violate them

## Minimum Bar

- CRITICAL findings: MUST fix before merge
- MAJOR findings: fix or document as accepted tech debt with justification
- MINOR findings: fix if cheap, otherwise note for future

## Anti-Slop Is Not Anti-Quality

Anti-slop targets structural inflation and AI-generated complexity. It does NOT mean:
- Removing all abstractions (justified abstractions stay)
- Inlining everything (DRY is real; shared code is good)
- Skipping error handling (contracts at boundaries are required)

The test: "Would a harsh maintainer who will own this for 2 years say 'I can work with this'?"
